newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: NSA seeks 30 pct earnings growth in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: NSA seeks 30 pct earnings growth in 1996/97.

text.p: NSA Investments Ltd would strive to achieve earnings growth of 30 percent or more in the year to end-June 1997, the South African investment trust said.
It was also considering holding a rights issue in the foreseeable future to fund further expansion, the group said following the release of its annual results on Wednesday.

"Our stated objective is to grow at 30 percent per annum," said Leonard Fine, the group's chief executive. "We will be satisfied if we achieve 30 percent, but this does not mean we will stop there," Fine told Reuters.

In a statement accompanying the results chairman Arnold Witkin said NSA was considering holding a rights issue to raise cash for further expansion as the group was enjoying a very good flow of quality investment opportunities.
Witkin was reticent to give details of any potential new investments but said: "We look for niche businesses with good management and above average growth prospects."
Fine would not say how much the proposed rights issue would raise.
In the year to June 30 NSA reported a 54 percent increase in earnings to 63 cents a share on attributable income of 33.54 million rand. No dividend was declared.

NSA recently raised its stake in South African air carrier Comair to 30 percent from 20. Comair in June announced an agency agreement with British Airways which will involve it trading under the U.K carrier's name and colours.
